proposal_reason:
ANALYSIS: Virchow2 (Prism2 slide embedding) is the strongest single model (0.860), clearly ahead of H-optimus-1 (0.830) and UNI2-h (0.821). Adding meta slightly hurts every model, so age/sex carry little signal. No fusion trials exist yet.
REASONING: Start with the method most likely to beat Virchow2 without overfitting: late_tuned, where each member runs at its own best setting. Combining with mean_prob is the simplest, lowest-variance way to test whether the three models carry complementary errors. If it works, it sets a robust reference point. Learned weights and stacking can be tested afterwards.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.865-0.875 AUROC if the models are complementary. If it scores at or below Virchow2's 0.86, the weaker members are diluting it. That would point to learned_weights or early_tuned with block weighting, which can down-weight or drop the weaker models.

ANALYSIS: late_tuned mean_prob (0.854) is slightly below the best single model, virchow2 (0.860; 0.859 with meta). Equal averaging dilutes Virchow2 with the weaker UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 members. Virchow2's strength is a low-dimensional, heavily regularized slide embedding (PCA16, C=0.001).
REASONING: This is still the exploration phase, so I want to map the methods. early_tuned learns a weight for each block inside the training fold. It can down-weight or drop the weaker blocks while keeping complementary signal, which a plain average cannot do. I chose C=0.01 because it is the shared C of the UNI and H-optimus members. Virchow2's PCA16 block is small, so it should still contribute at that C. meta_weight=1 because metadata alone is weak (0.599) and adding it slightly hurt every single-model baseline.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.86-0.87 AUROC, which would show that block weighting recovers Virchow2's dominance and adds a little complementary signal. If the result is at or below 0.855, joint early fusion over these blocks gains nothing at this C. I would then try other C values or late_tuned learned_weights/stack.

ANALYSIS: Virchow2 alone (0.860) is the strongest; equal-weight late fusion (0.854) and early_tuned (0.857) do not beat it, which suggests UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 add little or dilute Virchow2. Per-class weak spots are Lepidic and Papillary. Gated, plain early and the learned late combiners are still untested.
REASONING: In the exploration phase I want to map the methods. late_tuned with learned_weights can down-weight the weaker members, and it contains the best single model as a special case. It tests directly whether any weighting beats Virchow2-dominant fusion. It is cheap, uses only one knob, and answers whether non-uniform weighting matters.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.858-0.865, likely with weights concentrated on Virchow2. If it is no better than mean_prob, simple reweighting of the probability outputs does not help. Then fusion gains would have to come from feature-level interaction (early with balance_blocks or PCA) or from stacking.

ANALYSIS: Virchow2 (Prism slide embedding) dominates; mean_prob fusion (0.854) slightly underperforms virchow2 alone (0.860), suggesting the weaker mean-embedding models dilute it. learned_weights (0.864) nearly passed threshold, consistent with upweighting virchow2. Early_tuned at C=0.01 gave 0.857, no clear gain.
REASONING: Exploration phase: map untested methods. Plain early fusion with balance_blocks, L2 norm and PCA 32 per model, plus moderate C, tests whether a shared low-dimensional representation beats per-model members. Balancing blocks prevents UNI/H-optimus (more PCA variance) from swamping virchow2. C=0.01 is in the range that worked for members.
EXPECTED: Expect ~0.85-0.87. If it beats #1 by >0.013 the shared early concatenation is useful; if not, early-with-shared-knobs is no better than tuned variants, and focus shifts to stacking/gated or late with virchow-favoring weights.

ANALYSIS: Virchow2 alone (0.860) beats all fusions so far except learned_weights late_tuned (0.864), which likely mostly up-weights Virchow2. Equal-weight fusion (mean_prob) dilutes Virchow2 with the weaker UNI2/H-optimus members. Early fusion with shared PCA/C underperforms. Gated and stacking remain untested.
REASONING: Stacking on the tuned members' log-probabilities lets a second-level model learn per-class reliance on each model, e.g. using UNI/H-optimus where they complement Virchow2 (Papillary, Lepidic). Strong regularisation (stack_C=0.01) is appropriate given 134 training patients and 21 stack inputs. This also maps an untested combiner during exploration.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.865-0.875, possibly clearing the threshold over #1. If it lands at or below 0.86, per-class complementarity is too weak to learn at this sample size, and fusion gains will come only from weighting toward Virchow2.

ANALYSIS: Virchow2 alone (0.860) is the strongest; fusions so far sit around it (0.845-0.864) and none clearly beats the accepted best (mean_prob 0.854). Learned weights came closest (+0.0099), probably by up-weighting Virchow2. Equal averaging and early concatenation seem to dilute Virchow2 with the weaker UNI/H-optimus members. Gated and plain late with shared settings are untested.
REASONING: Exploration should map the untested methods. Gated is the most different fusion: a per-patient gate could lean on Virchow2 while still drawing on the others for the classes where they help. To limit overfitting with 134 patients I use PCA 32, L2 normalisation, small hidden size, strong dropout and weight decay, and a modest number of epochs.
EXPECTED: Likely AUROC around 0.84-0.86. If it clearly exceeds 0.865, adaptive gating is worth tuning. If it falls below about 0.85, I will drop gated and focus on late_tuned weighting variants (mean_logit, weighted_vote) and early_tuned C/meta_weight.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has yet beaten virchow2 alone (0.860). late_tuned with learned_weights came closest (0.8636, +0.0099 against a threshold of 0.0110). Early concatenation, stacking and gating all landed at 0.845-0.857, which suggests the weaker UNI2/H-optimus blocks add noise rather than complementary signal. The shared-setting 'late' method is still untested.
REASONING: This maps the last untested method family. Virchow2 preferred strong shrinkage (C=0.001, PCA 16, no L2). A shared low-dimensional, heavily regularised setting may also suit UNI2-h and H-optimus at this sample size, giving less overfit and more diverse members than their tuned PCA-128 configs. learned_weights was the best combiner so far, so I pair it with this setting.
EXPECTED: If heavy shrinkage helps the weaker members, AUROC should be about 0.865 or higher and could clear the threshold over trial #1. If it lands around 0.85, then shared low-dimensional settings do not help, the members carry little complementary signal, and the remaining budget should go to late_tuned/early_tuned variants (for example early_tuned at C=0.001).

ANALYSIS: Every fusion so far lands at 0.845-0.864, and none clearly beats Virchow2 alone (0.860). The best is late_tuned learned_weights at 0.8636, which probably leans mostly on Virchow2. Early_tuned at C=0.01 gave 0.857. Virchow2's own tuned C is 0.001, while UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 suit 0.01. Papillary (~0.73-0.77) and Lepidic (~0.76-0.80) are the weak classes in every trial.
REASONING: Early_tuned has only been tried at one C. With block weights learned by inner CV, a stronger shared penalty (C=0.001) matches Virchow2's optimum. The weaker blocks can still contribute through their weights, and with 134 patients the regularization level is the knob most likely to move AUROC. This maps the C direction for the joint linear model while still in exploration.
EXPECTED: If heavier shrinkage suits the concatenated model, AUROC should rise to about 0.865-0.87, with gains in Papillary and Lepidic. If it falls below 0.855, the early_tuned path is likely saturated or prefers a weaker penalty (C=0.1 would be the next check). I would then focus on late_tuned combine variants such as mean_logit or weighted_vote.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion method lands at 0.845-0.864 AUROC, no better than virchow2 alone (0.860). The best fusions (learned_weights at 0.8636, early_tuned with C=0.001 at 0.8611) probably lean almost entirely on Virchow2. The accepted best is #1 (mean_prob, 0.8537), which is weak, so a clear gain over it needs roughly +0.011-0.013.
REASONING: We are still in exploration. The untested combine rules are mean_logit and weighted_vote. mean_logit (geometric mean) sharpens agreement between the members and often beats mean_prob in calibrated ensembles. It also costs nothing: no inner CV, so there is no selection noise from learning weights on only 134 patients. It answers whether equal-weight fusion with a different pooling rule helps, as opposed to Virchow2 dominance.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.855-0.862, a small gain over mean_prob that probably falls short of the threshold. If it is no better than mean_prob, equal-weight late fusion adds nothing over the best single model. Remaining effort would then go to early_tuned at lower C or higher meta_weight, or to learned_weights variants.

ANALYSIS: All fusions cluster at 0.85-0.864, at or just above virchow2 alone (0.860). Learned_weights in late_tuned (0.8636) and early_tuned with stronger shrinkage (C=0.001, 0.8611) are best, but neither clears the noise threshold over #1. Equal-weight averaging hurts because UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 are weaker than Virchow2. Gated and stacking add variance without gain.
REASONING: Early_tuned improved when C went from 0.01 to 0.001, so the trend points toward stronger shrinkage. C=0.0001 checks whether the optimum lies further along that direction. It uses the last exploration slot on the open question in the most promising method family.
EXPECTED: Either a further gain toward ~0.865, possibly accepted against #1's 0.8537, or a drop from underfitting. If it drops, then C≈0.001 is the optimum for early_tuned. Fusion would then appear capped near Virchow2's level, and later trials should focus on meta_weight or the learned_weights variants.

ANALYSIS: Fusion clusters at 0.851-0.864 AUROC and has not clearly beaten Virchow2 alone (0.860). The current best, #1 (0.8537), is a weak anchor. Learned_weights (#3, +0.0099) and early_tuned at C=0.001 (#8, +0.0073) came closest to acceptance but stayed below the threshold. Papillary (about 0.73-0.77) and Lepidic (about 0.76-0.80) are the persistent weak classes. Metadata adds little or slightly hurts.
REASONING: Plain early fusion has only been tried once (#4: L2, PCA 32, C=0.01), and it underperformed. Virchow2 does best with strong compression and shrinkage (no L2, PCA 16, C=0.001). This trial applies that regime to all three blocks, with block balancing so that no single model dominates. A low-dimensional joint model (48 features plus age/sex) is the configuration most likely to exploit complementary signal across models without overfitting 134 training patients per fold. It is also a distinct untested region of the early method.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.860-0.868 AUROC, with possible gains on Papillary and Lepidic. If it lands at or below about 0.86, that points to Virchow2 being the effective ceiling, with the other two models adding only redundant signal. In that case I would focus remaining trials on Virchow2-weighted late fusion (learned_weights variants) rather than joint early models.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.85-0.864, basically at the virchow2 single-model level (0.860). The best non-accepted results (learned_weights 0.8636, early_tuned C=0.001 0.8611) are close to the threshold against #1 (0.8537), but #1 itself is a weak anchor. Virchow2 appears to dominate, and the other models add little except perhaps for Cribriform and Micropapillary.
REASONING: The open untested knobs are weighted_vote and the stack_C setting for late_tuned, plus the meta_weight setting for early_tuned. Stack with a stronger stack_C (0.1) may let the second-level model exploit per-class strengths, for example the hoptimus model on Micropapillary and Cribriform. However, stack at 0.01 already gave low BA, which suggests underfitting at that level. Early_tuned at C=0.001 with meta_weight 3 is a cheap variation, but metadata hurt the single models. Weighted_vote is untested, yet vote-based probabilities tend to give poor AUROC. Of these options, stack with stack_C=0.1 is the most plausible route to a clear gain: it can learn class-specific model weights, which learned_weights cannot.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC around 0.86-0.87, with a possible gain over #1 above the ~0.012 threshold. If the result is ≤0.855, stacking is too noisy with 134 patients, and I will focus on learned_weights or early_tuned around C=0.001.

ANALYSIS: No fusion trial has clearly beaten the accepted best, #1 (0.8537). The best results so far are late_tuned learned_weights (#3, 0.8636, +0.0099 vs a 0.011 threshold) and early_tuned with C=0.001 (#8, 0.8611). Both are essentially at the level of virchow2 alone (0.8601), which suggests UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 add little beyond Virchow2. Stacking and voting-style combiners are worse, and shared-preprocessing early/late fusion has not helped.
REASONING: The gated method has been tried only once (#6), with PCA 32 + L2 normalisation. That preprocessing is far from what suited Virchow2, the strongest member (no L2, PCA 16). A per-patient gate is the one mechanism here that could exploit cases where UNI2-h or H-optimus-1 help, for example Papillary and Lepidic, where all methods are weak. With PCA 16, no L2 and a small hidden size (16), there are few parameters for 134 training patients. That should cut the overfitting seen in #6 and lets the gate default toward Virchow2. This tests an open question rather than re-tuning the saturated logistic-regression fusions.
EXPECTED: If gating helps, AUROC should reach about 0.865–0.870 with gains in the Papillary/Lepidic per-class AUROCs, enough to clear the roughly 0.012 threshold over #1. If it lands around 0.85–0.86 again, I will conclude that the gated method adds nothing over linear fusion here. I would then spend the remaining trials on a few cheap checks around early_tuned/late_tuned, and otherwise accept that the fusion is capped near virchow2 alone.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has cleared the acceptance threshold. All trials sit at 0.845-0.864, and the best single model, virchow2 (0.860), is about as good as any fusion. The near-misses learned_weights (+0.0099) and early_tuned with C=0.001 (+0.0073) are both close to or include the virchow2-dominant solution. Stacking and gating are worse, and stacking gets worse as stack_C rises.
REASONING: Early_tuned is the most flexible linear fusion, because its block weights can drop or down-weight UNI2-h and H-optimus-1. Its C is now mapped: 0.001 is best, and 0.01 and 0.0001 are worse. The one untested knob is meta_weight. The UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 baselines were tuned with meta_weight=10, so less shrinkage of age/sex may help, especially for the weak Lepidic and Papillary classes. Testing meta_weight=3 at the best C answers that open question cheaply.
EXPECTED: I expect an AUROC of about 0.86-0.87. If it beats #1 by more than about 0.012 it is accepted. If it lands at or below 0.861, metadata weighting is not a lever, and early_tuned has plateaued at the level of virchow2 alone. In that case I would conclude that fusion adds little beyond Virchow2, and the remaining budget would go to stack with stack_C=0.001 and to the remaining late variants.

ANALYSIS: No fusion beats the best single model, Virchow2 (0.860). The best fusion results (late_tuned learned_weights 0.864, early_tuned C=0.001 0.861) only tie it. They were rejected against the weak incumbent #1 (0.854), because the paired-gain thresholds are about 0.011-0.013. Stacking, gated networks and balanced early fusion with PCA of 16 or 32 all came out at or below 0.85. Lepidic and Papillary (about 0.75-0.79) are the weak classes in every method.
REASONING: An open question is whether per-model PCA throws away signal in early fusion. Every early trial so far used PCA 16 or 32 with block balancing. Strongly regularised full-dimensional concatenation is untested: L2 per slide, no PCA, C=0.0001, no balancing. In that setup Virchow2's 2560 columns naturally carry more weight, matching it being the strongest model. The ridge-like shrinkage can still pick up the complementary UNI2/H-optimus signal for classes such as Cribriform and Micropapillary. This tests a different region of the space from the near-duplicate early_tuned and late_tuned variants.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.86-0.87. If it exceeds 0.8537 by more than about 0.013 it is accepted. If it lands at or below 0.86, the conclusion is that fusion adds no detectable value over Virchow2 at this sample size. I would then make one or two final checks (late_tuned weighted_vote, early_tuned with meta_weight=10) and accept that the search stops.

ANALYSIS: All fusion variants cluster at 0.845-0.864, essentially the level of the best single model (virchow2 0.860). Every gain over the accepted best (#1, 0.8537) has fallen below its threshold (best: learned_weights at +0.0099 vs 0.0110). The evidence suggests that Virchow2 carries most of the signal and that UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 add little complementary information. Papillary (~0.75) and Lepidic (~0.78) remain the weak classes under every method.
REASONING: Untested regions that could plausibly give a clear gain: early fusion without L2, with no PCA or a large PCA, and at very strong regularisation. #15 (L2, no PCA, C=1e-4) reached 0.860 with low fold SD, the closest any untested-style method has come. Its neighbour PCA=128 with balance_blocks=True would keep most of the information while equalising the blocks, and the low SD of #15 may help shrink the corrected SE. Other open options are weak: late_tuned weighted_vote is unlikely to beat learned_weights, and the stack variants were worse. I therefore probe early fusion with L2, PCA 128, balanced blocks and C=1e-4.
EXPECTED: I expect about 0.858-0.866. That is likely still below the threshold, though it could be accepted if the paired variance is low. If it fails, that supports the view that fusion offers no clear gain over the best single model here. I would then spend only a few more trials, such as late_tuned weighted_vote or early_tuned at C=0.001 with meta_weight=10, before accepting that conclusion.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.85-0.864 AUROC, roughly the level of virchow2 alone (0.860). The best result, late_tuned learned_weights at 0.8636, missed acceptance by a hair. Strongly regularised early fusion on L2-normalised full features (#15, #16) gave the lowest fold SDs (0.026) at about 0.860. Gated and stacking are consistently worse, and Papillary and Lepidic remain the weak classes.
REASONING: This is an untested combination of the two most promising signals. It runs late fusion with learned simplex weights, which came closest, on the heavily shrunk, L2-normalised, no-PCA members that gave the most stable early-fusion folds. Lower per-fold variance shrinks the corrected SE, which lowers the bar for acceptance. Learned weights can also down-weight uni2h and hoptimus1 if they are weak in this regime.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.862-0.868 with fold SD near 0.027, which could clear the roughly 0.011 threshold over #1. If it stays at about 0.860, then late fusion is capped by virchow2 whatever the member regularisation. In that case I would try the remaining cheap options (late_tuned weighted_vote, stack_C=0.001) before concluding that fusion adds nothing beyond virchow2.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at 0.845-0.864, and none is clearly above Virchow2 alone (0.860). The accepted best (#1 mean_prob, 0.8537) is itself below Virchow2. The strongest results come from the learned_weights combine (#3 0.8636, #17 0.8626) and from strongly regularised early fusion (C≤0.001, ~0.860). Stacking, gating and balance_blocks never helped. Papillary (~0.75) and Lepidic (~0.78) remain the weak classes in every method.
REASONING: learned_weights twice came close to the threshold (+0.0099 and +0.0088). It can down-weight the weaker UNI2/H-optimus members while keeping complementary signal. #17 used L2 norm, no PCA and C=0.0001. One step less shrinkage (C=0.001) is the untested neighbour most likely to sharpen each member while staying in the strong-regularisation regime that worked for early fusion and for Virchow2. This is a targeted try at clearing the ~0.011 threshold.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.864-0.868, which could clear the threshold against #1. If it again lands near 0.862 or is rejected, then learned-weight late fusion has plateaued at roughly Virchow2-alone level. I would then conclude that the extra models add little beyond Virchow2 and spend the remaining trials on the few untested combines (weighted_vote, early_tuned with meta_weight=10) rather than fine-tuning C.

ANALYSIS: All fusion trials cluster at 0.845–0.864 AUROC, roughly the virchow2-alone ceiling of 0.860. The closest calls are late_tuned learned_weights (+0.0099 vs a 0.0110 threshold) and early_tuned / early with strong shrinkage (+0.006–0.007). Stacking got worse as stack_C rose (0.01 → 0.8510, 0.1 → 0.8467), and stacking also lowered balanced accuracy. Gated nets and balanced-block early fusion did not help.
REASONING: Stacking at stack_C=0.001 is the one untested end of a knob that showed a monotone trend. Very strong shrinkage pulls the stacker toward an averaged log-probability combiner with learned class biases, while still letting it lean on virchow2 per class (Papillary and Lepidic are the weak classes). It is the cheapest open question left that could plausibly beat the mean_prob best by more than the threshold. The other untested options look unpromising: weighted_vote gives coarse probabilities, which suits AUROC poorly, and gated variants have underperformed twice.
EXPECTED: Expect about 0.857–0.865 AUROC with better balanced accuracy than stack_C=0.01. If it does not clear the threshold, stacking is exhausted. I would then conclude that fusion cannot reliably exceed the virchow2 signal on 167 patients, and spend the remaining trials only on near-threshold variants such as early_tuned with meta_weight=10.

ANALYSIS: Nearly every reasonable fusion lands around 0.858-0.864 AUROC. That is roughly Virchow2 alone (0.860), and gains over the accepted best (#1, 0.8537) reach about +0.01 but never clear the threshold of about 0.011-0.017. Stacking and gating are clearly worse, especially with strong stack shrinkage. early_tuned at C=0.001 is among the strongest and most stable configurations: meta_weight 1 gave 0.8611 and meta_weight 3 gave 0.8604.
REASONING: early_tuned at C=0.001 is the most consistent configuration so far. The one knob not yet tried there is meta_weight=10, the setting the UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 members preferred on their own. A larger meta weight removes shrinkage on age/sex while the image blocks stay heavily regularised. This is a cheap, focused test of whether metadata adds signal through fusion; meta alone scores 0.599, so it carries some information.
EXPECTED: Most likely about 0.860-0.866, near the plateau, with a possible small gain on Lepidic and Papillary. If it does not clear the threshold, I will conclude that metadata weighting is saturated and that fusion cannot reliably beat Virchow2 on this data. The remaining budget should then go to only a few distinct questions, such as weighted_vote or a weakly regularised stack, before accepting the plateau.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion lands at about 0.85–0.863 AUROC, close to the Virchow2-only baseline (0.860). No trial has cleared the noise threshold over the weak accepted best (#1, mean_prob, 0.8537). The strongest results all let Virchow2 dominate: learned_weights (#3 0.8636, #17 0.8626), early_tuned at C=0.001 (#8 0.8611), and L2 plus strong shrinkage (#15). Stacking, gated networks and uniform averaging are worse, so the extra models add little signal beyond Virchow2.
REASONING: Only 5 trials remain before the stop rule, so the best bet is the region nearest the threshold: late learned_weights. #3 missed by 0.001, and #17/#18 (L2, no PCA) came close. Untested here is per-model L2 plus PCA 128 with C=0.001. PCA 128 was the tuned setting for UNI2-h and H-optimus-1, so it may strengthen those members while learned weights stay free to favour Virchow2. This could add the roughly 0.01 needed, with lower fold variance.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.862–0.866, with a paired gain over #1 of about 0.010–0.013, possibly just above threshold. If it is again rejected, fusion offers no reliable gain over Virchow2 alone on this data. I would then spend the remaining trials only on untested combine rules (e.g. late_tuned weighted_vote) and otherwise accept that the search has converged.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion variant lands at 0.85-0.863 AUROC, about the virchow2 single-model level (0.860). The accepted best (#1, 0.8537) is weak, but no gain over it has cleared the threshold (0.011-0.018). The best so far are #3 late_tuned learned_weights (+0.0099 vs a 0.0110 threshold) and #17 late learned_weights (+0.0088). Fusion appears to add little beyond Virchow2; Papillary and Lepidic stay hard for every model.
REASONING: With 4 trials left before the stop, the best chance of a clear gain is a configuration not yet tried that could beat #1 on most folds. Options: weighted_vote in late_tuned is untested, but voting usually hurts AUROC. Late with learned_weights at C=0.0001, PCA 16 and L2 off is a variant of #7/#17. The early_tuned C=0.01 point gave 0.8566, so that method is mapped. Late_tuned stack with stack_C=1.0 is the last untested stack setting, but stacking got worse as stack_C rose from 0.01 to 0.1, so it is unpromising. Late l2=True, pca=64, C=0.01, learned_weights (stronger per-model fits for UNI/H-optimus) is reasonable. Better: late mean_prob with l2=True, pca=None, C=0.0001, a strongly shrunk shared setting that may average cleanly. Since #17 at C=0.0001 nearly cleared the bar with learned_weights, mean_logit at the same setting tests whether a fixed average without inner-CV noise has lower variance and so passes the paired SE threshold.
EXPECTED: AUROC around 0.860-0.865, with gains more consistent across folds than learned_weights gave, possibly clearing the ~0.011 threshold. If it fails, fusion offers no reliable gain over Virchow2 alone. The remaining trials should then go to confirming that and not to fine-tuning C.

ANALYSIS: After 22 trials no fusion has cleared the acceptance threshold over trial #1 (0.8537). Every reasonable method sits at 0.857-0.864, which is about the level of the best single model (virchow2, 0.860). The closest misses all used learned_weights (late_tuned #3 at +0.0099 against a 0.0110 threshold, late #17 at +0.0088). Stacking, mean_logit and gated are consistently worse, and early_tuned has plateaued near 0.861 across C and meta_weight.
REASONING: Only 3 trials remain before the stop rule, so the best use is the least-explored region near the strongest family. The late method with learned_weights has only been tried at C ≤ 0.001. However, uni2h and hoptimus1 were tuned at C=0.01 with L2 normalisation, so C=0.01 with l2=True and no PCA should strengthen those members. That makes them more useful partners for virchow2 in the learned weighting, while keeping the method that came closest to acceptance.
EXPECTED: I expect roughly 0.862-0.868 AUROC, with possible gains on Acinar and Micropapillary. If the gain again falls below the threshold, the evidence says fusion cannot reliably beat virchow2 alone on 167 patients. The remaining trials would then only be confirming a plateau, and virchow2(+meta), or the simplest fusion, should be reported as the practical choice.

ANALYSIS: Every fusion variant falls between 0.845 and 0.864 AUROC, which is the level of the best single model (virchow2 0.860, virchow2+meta 0.859). None has cleared the acceptance threshold over the weak incumbent #1 (0.854). The best results come from learned_weights (#3 0.8636, #17 0.8626) and from early_tuned with heavy shrinkage (#8 0.8611). These suggest fusion mostly falls back to virchow2, and the complementary signal from UNI2-h and H-optimus-1 is small. Stacking and gating are clearly worse, and meta_weight has little effect.
REASONING: Only 2 trials remain before the stop rule fires, so the next trial should be the one most likely to clear the ~0.011-0.013 threshold. Untested regions near the best results are: weighted_vote, late with pca=16 using other combiners, and early_tuned at C=0.1. early_tuned at larger C lets the inner-CV block weights do the shrinkage (C x w^2) rather than the global C. It is untested, but the trend from C=0.001 down to 0.0001 points the wrong way for larger C. Late with L2 normalisation, no PCA, C=0.0001 and mean_prob is a smooth, robust ensemble under strong regularisation. However, mean_logit with that setting was weak (0.847), so mean_prob probably lands around 0.855. I choose early_tuned with meta_weight=1 and C=0.1: it is the one untested axis of the best-calibrated method, and it answers whether a looser global penalty combined with learned block weights adds signal.
EXPECTED: Most likely AUROC of 0.850-0.862, rejected. If it reaches about 0.866 or higher with low fold SD, it could be accepted. If it fails, I conclude that fusion gives no reliable gain over virchow2 on this data, and the final choice should be learned_weights fusion or the single virchow2 model.

ANALYSIS: No fusion has cleared the acceptance threshold. The strongest trials, late_tuned learned_weights (0.8636, +0.0099 vs threshold 0.0110) and early_tuned C=0.001 (0.8611), only match Virchow2 alone (0.8601). Stacking, mean_logit and gated networks are consistently worse. All methods share the same per-class pattern: Lepidic and Papillary stay weak (~0.75-0.79), and fusion never fixes them.
REASONING: This is the last trial before the stop rule fires, so it should either give a plausible clear gain or close an open question. Within the strongest family (late_tuned, where each member runs at its own best setting), weighted_vote is the only combiner not yet tried. Learned_weights came closest to acceptance, so a combiner that also gives the members unequal weights is the most plausible remaining candidate. Re-tuning C or meta_weight in the other families has plateaued at about 0.86.
EXPECTED: I expect AUROC of roughly 0.855-0.864, most likely below the threshold. If a voting-type combiner reaches the 0.865+ range, it is accepted. If it fails, I conclude that on 167 patients the three-model fusion gives no gain over Virchow2 alone that can be told apart from noise. In that case the Virchow2(+meta) baseline, or the simplest late_tuned fusion, should be carried forward.
